heading: What the world model predicted and what happened
intro: In these tasks a round pusher pushes a block onto a marked goal pose without grasping it. Each of the 17 programs the Code-as-Policies (CaP) agent wrote was run for 200 episodes inside the world model and 50 in the environment. Select a program to see its results, and click any episode mark to replay that episode. Try v5 (the version the agent submitted, 20% in the world model, 16% in the environment) and then v4 (98%, 96%).

card_short_description: Browse recorded runs in world model and environment
card_body:
An interactive companion to [World Models as Unit Tests](https://dongzhezheng.github.io/world-models-as-unit-tests/). The first panel replays 17 pushing programs from the [Code as Policies](https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.07753) (CaP) agent in the world model and in the environment, with per-episode replay. The second panel compares the CaP agent and the world-model agent on a hand-and-screwdriver task after 5 and 15 real trials. Code and full results are in the [repository](https://github.com/DongzheZheng/world-models-as-unit-tests).

The CaP agent is modelled on [ASPIRE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00272). The note draws on earlier work that writes world models as code: [Code World Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15383), [WorldCoder](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.12275), [CWM](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.02387), [Code as Worlds](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27549) and [Code World Model](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25927).
hand_heading: A four-fingered hand tightens a screw
hand_intro: A Panda arm with a four-fingered Allegro hand holds a free precision screwdriver and tightens a left-handed screw in MuJoCo by rolling the handle between its fingertips and regrasping. An episode succeeds when the retained torque ends between 0.050 and 0.086 N·m with the screw undamaged and the tool still in the hand; the thread strips at 0.125 N·m. The agents get no force or torque reading and cannot see the screw while the tool is on it. Two agents (both Claude Opus 5.5) each wrote a program after 5 real trials and again after 15. The Code as Policies (CaP) agent edits its program after each trial. The world-model agent writes a world model as one Python file (350 lines at 5 trials, 390 at 15) and tests its program there. Select a stage, then click a held-out mark to play its video.
